title: Open stabilizer-isomorphism locus for representable etale maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, and 2-fibre products have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a stack $\mathcal A$, its inertia $I_{\mathcal A}(T)$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows $v:(a,\alpha)\to(b,\beta)$ with $v\alpha=\beta v$. The projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a scheme finite over its base [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The point space $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a scheme atlas. A geometric stabilizer at a point is the automorphism group algebraic space of a representative over an algebraically closed field; comparison means comparison after a common algebraically closed field extension. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale map between Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$, and assume $\mathcal B$ has finite inertia. The subset $W\subseteq|\mathcal A|$ where $f$ induces an isomorphism of geometric stabilizer group algebraic spaces is open. There is a strictly full open substack $\mathcal A^\circ\subseteq\mathcal A$ with point space $W$, and the canonical map $I_{\mathcal A^\circ}\longrightarrow\mathcal A^\circ\times_{\mathcal B}I_{\mathcal B}$ is an isomorphism. An open substack is a full substack stable under pullback whose base change by any scheme is an open subscheme. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. In particular, every point where the stabilizers are isomorphic belongs to this open substack.

source.place: Tag 0DUA (lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified), specialized to representable etale maps and finite target inertia (finite is proper).

proof.text: Fix any $S$-scheme $T$ and $a\in\mathcal A(T)$. Write $H=\operatorname{Aut}_T(fa)$ and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_T(a)$ as sheaves on $T$-schemes. By the finite-inertia hypothesis $H$ is a scheme finite over $T$. Put $X=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B,fa}T$. Representability and etaleness of $f$ say exactly that $X$ is an algebraic space etale over $T$. On a test $T'\to T$, an object of $X$ is $(b,\lambda:fb\xrightarrow{\sim}fa|_{T'})$; an arrow $v:(b,\lambda)\to(b',\lambda')$ satisfies $\lambda' f(v)=\lambda$. The identity gives a section $s:T\to X$. Over $H$, its universal automorphism $\alpha$ gives the section $t_\alpha=(a,\alpha^{-1})$. Thus the pullback of $\Delta_{X/T}$ by $(s,t_\alpha):H\to X\times_T X$ is $G\to H$: an isomorphism $s\to t_\alpha$ is precisely a $v\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$ with $f(v)=\alpha$. This computation is natural in $T'$; uniqueness holds because $X$ is an algebraic space, hence its groupoids have no nonidentity automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified, proof; direct diagonal description of its inertia comparison as in remark-get-property-auts-from-diagonal.

proof.text: The etale algebraic-space morphism $X\to T$ is unramified by [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence]. Apply [lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal] to this map and to the scheme test $H\to X\times_T X$ constructed in step 1. It says that $j_T:G\to H$ is represented by an open subscheme of $H$. In particular the stabilizer comparison is an open immersion, for every scheme $T\to\mathcal A$, and the same description applies after every further scheme base change. No separatedness of $f$ or flatness of either inertia projection is used.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified, proof; direct diagonal description of its inertia comparison as in remark-get-property-auts-from-diagonal.

proof.text: Choose an etale surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal A$. Apply steps 1--2 with its object $a$ to obtain an open subscheme $G\subset H$ and a finite scheme map $q:H\to U$. Set $C=|H|\setminus|G|$. The finite-map theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] makes $q(C)$ closed. The inverse image of $W$ in $U$ is exactly $U\setminus q(C)$. Indeed the comparison over a geometric point $\bar u$ is the base change $G_{\bar u}\subset H_{\bar u}$. It is an isomorphism exactly when that open subscheme is the whole fibre [def-weil-open-immersion]. If $C$ has a point over $u$, take an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; the resulting geometric point of $H$ is still outside $G$, so the geometric comparison fails. Conversely, a missing geometric point of the open fibre maps to a point of $C$ over $u$. This also proves independence of the chosen geometric representative: a nonempty complement remains nonempty after extension to a common algebraically closed field, whereas an isomorphism remains an isomorphism. Thus $p^{-1}(W)$ is open.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified, proof; direct diagonal description of its inertia comparison as in remark-get-property-auts-from-diagonal.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-topology-open-substacks], openness is detected on the etale surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal A$. Step 3 therefore proves that $W$ is open in $|\mathcal A|$. The same node's open-substack/open-subset bijection supplies a strictly full open substack $\mathcal A^\circ\subseteq\mathcal A$ with point space $W$. Its pullback clause says that every geometric point of a scheme $T\to\mathcal A^\circ$ maps into $W$.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified, proof; direct diagonal description of its inertia comparison as in remark-get-property-auts-from-diagonal.

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal A^\circ$ with object $a$, step 2 identifies $j_T:\operatorname{Aut}_T(a)\to\operatorname{Aut}_T(fa)$ with an open subscheme of the finite $T$-scheme $H$. Its complement is empty: a point of that complement would, after passage to an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], give a geometric point of $T$ at which the stabilizer map is not an isomorphism, contradicting step 4. Hence $j_T$ is an isomorphism by the definition of open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Strict fullness identifies automorphisms of $a$ in $\mathcal A^\circ$ and $\mathcal A$. Consequently every object $(a,\alpha)$ of $\mathcal A^\circ\times_{\mathcal B}I_{\mathcal B}$ has a unique lift $(a,\beta)$ with $f\beta=\alpha$. The lift commutes with pullback by uniqueness. If $v:a\to b$ conjugates $\alpha$ to $\alpha'$, then $v\beta v^{-1}$ and $\beta'$ have the same image under the injective stabilizer map at $b$, so they are equal. Thus the lift also respects all arrows and gives an inverse to the canonical inertia map. This proves its asserted isomorphism. Finally every stabilizer-isomorphism point belongs to $\mathcal A^\circ$ because its point space is exactly $W$.
